approach: A stateless provider evaluates the engine-composed frozen initial input. Caller submits the full unchanged canonical profile. At start Loop Engine may add its allocated artifact_root when absent, preserving every submitted profile field; it freezes the composed value, which show and evaluate project unchanged. No provider catalog or mutable policy lookup is permitted. Flat describe accepts only operation and optional opaque initial_input, ignores the optional value and returns the exact unchanged static workflow topology. A bounded generic checker supplies exhaustive deterministic structural violations before independent external-evidence aggregation. Canonical templates/reviewer protocol are inspectable versioned data with exact-byte parity, not required undeclared initial_input fields.

elements.name: protocol boundary
elements.responsibility: Parse one strict request, dispatch describe or evaluate, and emit one strict result with the defined exit taxonomy.

elements.name: generic schema checker
elements.responsibility: Validate only the allowlisted schema subset and return deterministic exhaustive violations without knowing workflow subjects.

elements.name: evidence evaluator
elements.responsibility: Attribute, conform, supersede, and judge external evidence against configured axes without reading files or judging truth.

elements.name: versioned data profiles
elements.responsibility: Supply selected run's frozen policies, schemas, prompts, templates, and reviewer protocol as inspectable reference data outside provider judging code; no profile catalog is hard-coded in design. The host design-artifact review schema is a separate contract from the fictional runtime profiles governed by this bounded language.

elements.name: checked transition evaluator
elements.responsibility: Consume deterministic exhaustive structural violations from the generic schema checker and map each named violation into checked-transition denial details before or without evidence satisfaction; then apply the configured evidence gate and permit the reference workflow terminal transition only after configured validation obligations pass.

decisions.choice: Keep revision linkage in a separate config declaration.
decisions.rationale: Cross-artifact equality is needed by this workflow but is not a generic schema keyword.
rejected: Embedding a workflow-specific keyword in the generic checker.

decisions.choice: Freeze one bounded schema language shared by the generic checker and versioned data profiles: types object, array, and string; object keywords additionalProperties, properties, required, and type; array keywords items, minItems, and type; string keywords enum, minLength, and type. additionalProperties must be false (literal false only); unknown keywords and invalid keyword placement are rejected; instance checking collects every applicable violation in deterministic path/rule order.
decisions.rationale: The schema checker and shipped profile schemas consume one inspectable contract, so callers get exhaustive structural denial without full JSON Schema or workflow-specific interpretation.
rejected: Full JSON Schema and its unneeded keyword surface.
A second custom artifact language or profile-specific schema dialect.

decisions.choice: Treat author identity as the exact name-kind pair and exclude the subject author.
decisions.rationale: Evidence aggregation needs deterministic distinctness and independence while preserving external claims.
rejected: Cryptographic identity or provider-side author allowlists.

decisions.choice: Preserve exact provider protocol contract: flat describe request has required operation:"describe" and only optional opaque initial_input; accept and ignore that optional input for static description and reject every other unknown field; flat evaluate request fields operation, workflow, initial_input, context, transition, prior_evaluations; reject unknown fields; describe returns workflow; evaluate returns exactly {"result":"allow"}, {"result":"unsupported"}, or {"result":"deny","feedback":{"code","message","details"?}}; exit 0 means valid response written, 1 evaluation/config failure with stderr/no stdout response, 2 protocol/usage failure with stderr/no stdout response; one request/process.
decisions.rationale: Compatibility with the existing Loop Engine provider boundary requires one local subprocess per request and forbids changing the reference workflow state or transition topology. Recording this exact contract gives the plan worker a complete protocol boundary and leaves no request, response, exit, or process behavior to invent.
rejected: Adding nested request envelopes or extra request fields.
Allowing unknown fields or multiple requests in one process.
Changing response variants or exit meanings to fit an implementation preference.

decisions.choice: Caller submits the full unchanged canonical profile. At start Loop Engine may add its allocated artifact_root when absent, preserving every submitted profile field; it freezes the composed value, which show and evaluate project unchanged. No provider catalog or mutable policy lookup is permitted.
decisions.rationale: The existing engine performs artifact-root allocation before freezing, preserving canonical obligations; show/evaluate expose the immutable composed value without provider environment/catalog drift.
rejected: Resolving profile identifier through provider catalog/environment.
Loading mutable repository profile at evaluation.

decisions.choice: Freeze evidence aggregation by exact gate, policy axis, subject, subject_revision, config_version, and author (name, kind): only current subject revision and frozen config version can satisfy; subject author is excluded; latest conforming verdict per exact (axis, current subject revision, author identity) stands; every required distinct non-subject author must be present with zero standing fails, and duplicate records from one author do not increase author count; malformed or nonconforming current-axis records block until a later conforming record for the same gate and axis supersedes them. Provider evaluates supplied claims deterministically but does not authenticate identity or judge semantic truth.
decisions.rationale: This prevents stale, duplicate, or self-authored evidence from laundering obligation satisfaction while preserving a deterministic provider boundary for external semantic judgment.
rejected: Vote counting, which could let repeated or opposing claims launder a standing obligation.
Accepting stale or config-mismatched evidence, which could replay judgment against obsolete subjects or obligations.
Counting duplicate records from one author, which would counterfeit independent author coverage.
Provider-side identity authentication or semantic judging, which would cross the external-judgment boundary.

risks.risk: An author may edit an artifact materially without changing its declared revision.
risks.mitigation: The external actor must bump the revision and obtain renewed review for material edits; recheck the current declared artifact at every approval boundary. The provider still trusts declared revisions and cannot detect dishonest same-revision edits. Only the intent's immaterial-edit residual is accepted; no hashing, locking, or provider-side semantic enforcement is added.

risks.risk: A shipped profile may contain an unsupported bounded-schema keyword or revision-link mismatch, making configured obligations unavailable or misapplied.
risks.mitigation: Deterministic startup/profile validation rejects unsupported schema keywords, malformed revision links, and missing configured obligation references before evaluation.

risks.risk: Exact name-kind declared identity is unauthenticated; a subject can claim another identity.
risks.mitigation: Provider preserves deterministic declared-identity checks; external process and provenance controls remain outside scope, so this residual is accepted.

coverage.acceptance: A caller can inspect the frozen policies and artifact schemas before evaluating a transition.
coverage.delivered_by: Caller submits the full unchanged canonical profile. At start Loop Engine may add its allocated artifact_root when absent, preserving every submitted profile field; it freezes the composed value, which show and evaluate project unchanged. No provider catalog or mutable policy lookup is permitted. Frozen policies and schemas are inspectable through show; canonical templates/reviewer-protocol are inspectable through versioned data exposure, preserving exact bytes.

coverage.acceptance: A malformed subject artifact is denied with each violated structural rule named.
coverage.delivered_by: Generic schema checker returns exhaustive violations; checked transition evaluator maps every exact path/rule into denial details before or without evidence satisfaction; evaluate.rs::schema_deny_reports_every_simultaneous_structural_violation proves that production relationship.

coverage.acceptance: A checked transition refuses stale, self-authored, duplicate-author, or configured-obligation-incomplete evidence.
coverage.delivered_by: Decision 6 freezes exact evidence attribution and standing-verdict semantics; evidence evaluator applies current-revision/config, subject-author, supersession, malformed-block, and distinct-author rules, and checked transition evaluator refuses incomplete results.

coverage.acceptance: The reference workflow reaches its terminal state only after its configured validation obligations are satisfied.
coverage.delivered_by: Checked transition evaluator maps the terminal gate to versioned data profile obligations and requires the configured validation axes.
